thesis: The latest ten transaction-bearing sessions were gross profitable by INR 3,259.11, but INR 8,129.25 of charges converted that into an INR 4,870.14 net loss. The clearest current admission problem is Rangebound entries below decision score 50: in the mandatory latest-seven window they lost INR 4,031.99 while score-50-or-higher Rangebound entries made INR 2,342.08. Exit opportunity is concentrated in signal-deterioration exits, but the day-close comparison is hindsight and does not justify globally loosening exits. Captured top-gainer evidence found only one missed candidate, IFCI on 2026-08-28, whose later observed peak exceeded the strategy's 1% net requirement; the broader top-gainer sample is too small to relax regime gates.

setupFindings.conclusion: Rangebound was gross profitable over ten sessions but became net negative after charges. In the latest seven sessions the loss is isolated to decision scores below 50. Five of six dates containing below-50 trades support a higher floor; 2026-08-31 contradicts it with INR 660.00 net from two below-50 trades.

The setup is a material drag, but five latest-seven positions across only three dates do not meet the minimum sample for a medium-confidence disable recommendation. Preserve the current enabled state while collecting more evidence.
Momentum Runner was slightly gross profitable but charges made it net negative. Its result is not poor enough, relative to sample and recent profitable trades, to justify disabling it.

exitFindings.conclusion: Signal-deterioration exits produced the largest hindsight gap: 13 of 18 would have had a better day-close price, including KENNAMET, QUESS, SUPRIYA, VIJAYA, and UFLEX. This is not proof that later exits were executable or safer. Stops had almost neutral signed day-close difference and time/no-progress exits protected more value than they forfeited, so neither should be broadly loosened.

topGainerAnalysis.conclusion: Top-five rank is only a candidate-pool label, not entry permission. Only nine of 171 stock-day appearances ever passed the dedicated continuation or pullback rules. Of seven qualified-but-unexecuted candidates, IFCI is the only one whose later observed peak cleared the 1% net-profit requirement. Thirty-five additional stocks later moved more than 1% net from a plausible triggered observation, but they had not satisfied the strategy's trend, extension, score, or regime requirements and must be treated as research hypotheses. Do not loosen the current top-gainer gates from this evidence alone.

newIndicators.name: leaderRankPersistencePct30m
newIndicators.definition: 100 times the number of valid snapshots ranked in the top five divided by valid candidate snapshots during the prior 30 minutes.
newIndicators.purpose: Separate persistent leaders from a one-snapshot ranking spike.

newIndicators.name: leaderRankStability30m
newIndicators.definition: Clamp 0-1 of 1 minus the standard deviation of top-gainer rank divided by 2 over the prior 30 minutes.
newIndicators.purpose: Prefer stocks that remain near the top rather than oscillating into and out of the pool.

newIndicators.name: recentHighRetestPct
newIndicators.definition: 100 times recentHigh minus livePrice divided by recentHigh.
newIndicators.purpose: Identify a controlled pullback from the impulse high without requiring a full VWAP touch.

newIndicators.name: emaSpreadSlope3Bars
newIndicators.definition: Three-completed-bar slope of 100 times EMA9 minus EMA20 divided by price.
newIndicators.purpose: Detect improving trend structure before the raw EMA crossover occurs.

newIndicators.name: triggerExtensionAtr
newIndicators.definition: Live price minus frozen entry trigger divided by ATR.
newIndicators.purpose: Normalize extension for stock volatility instead of relying only on a fixed percentage.

newIndicators.name: leaderReacceleration
newIndicators.definition: True when five-minute change is at least 0.1%, either three- or five-minute volume ratio is at least 1, and the current completed candle closes above the prior completed candle high.
newIndicators.purpose: Require renewed participation after the retest rather than buying a fading leader.

exitAndSelectionResearch.name: Rangebound signal-recovery observer
exitAndSelectionResearch.design: When a Rangebound trade reaches signal deterioration, record a shadow 15-minute recovery window. Observe whether a completed candle reclaims VWAP before the original stop is hit; do not delay the real exit yet.
exitAndSelectionResearch.evidence: Latest seven sessions contain 11 signal-deterioration exits across six dates. Eight had a better day-close price, with INR 11,452.15 signed aggregate day-close difference and positive support on five of six affected dates.
exitAndSelectionResearch.risk: Day-close improvement does not establish the price after 15 minutes or the adverse path before recovery, so changing the real exit is not justified.

exitAndSelectionResearch.design: Persist fallback ranking, rolling ordinary/sector capacity, top-N, duplicate-symbol, and sizing-to-zero causes directly in rejectionReasons.

limitations: This result is analytics-reviewed only. No Replay, backtest, parameter sweep, targeted setting trial, or setting mutation was run.
The ten-session review uses the latest ten dates containing reconciled positions, not ten calendar days.
The mandatory confidence window uses the latest seven transaction-bearing dates ending 2026-09-04 and contains all seven requested dates.

Day-close opportunity loss and later observed candidate peaks are hindsight benchmarks, not executable counterfactuals. They do not model whether an exit signal would still have been valid, intraperiod drawdown, queueing, fills, or an implementable peak exit.
The standardized top-gainer opportunity uses INR 50,000 exposure and modeled 0.107% transaction cost plus 0.06% slippage; it is a comparability benchmark, not claimed realizable profit.
Snapshot coverage was 91.03% overall. The selected day had 114 usable snapshots out of 191, so missed-candidate inference for 2026-09-04 is less complete than other dates.

Settings fingerprints changed around 2026-08-25, although the exact recommended Rangebound score key remained 40 throughout all ten sessions. Earlier sessions materially contradict the latest-seven below-50 split, so the recommendation is medium-confidence rather than high.

recommendations.description: Setup-specific decision-score floor for rangebound lower-bound entries.
recommendations.rationale: Raise the Rangebound admission floor from 40 to 50 to remove the current low-score subgroup whose losses and charges dominate recent setup economics.
evidence: Latest-seven affected group: 17 below-50 Rangebound positions across six dates, 3 wins, gross P/L INR -2,204.32, charges INR 1,827.67, net P/L INR -4,031.99, expectancy INR -237.18, profit factor 0.32.

Latest-seven unaffected group: 9 score-50-or-higher Rangebound positions across four dates, 4 wins, gross P/L INR 3,198.45, charges INR 856.37, net P/L INR 2,342.08, expectancy INR 260.23, profit factor 2.52.
Five of six latest-seven dates containing below-50 trades support the higher floor. The contradicting date is 2026-08-31, when two below-50 positions made INR 660.00 net.
The exact 40 score value and current-override source were present on all ten reviewed dates. The latest-seven settings fingerprint was stable from 2026-08-26 through 2026-09-04.
The change would also reject three latest-seven winners: ANANDRATHI INR 945.43, LODHA INR 873.99, and QUESS INR 72.23.
recommendations.risk: The score split is regime-sensitive. Across the full ten sessions, the first three dates contributed profitable below-50 trades, and the proposed floor would reject three recent winners totaling INR 1,891.65. It may reduce trade count sharply and miss mean-reversion winners, so it should be treated as analytics-reviewed, not validated.

validation.reason: The exact 40-to-50 mechanism was checked against 17 affected reconciled positions over six latest-seven dates. Aggregate evidence is favorable and five of six affected dates support it, meeting medium confidence, but no replay or targeted trial was run.
